title: A weather forecast that stopped advancing is read as a recovery: published fresh while every row lies in the past
claim: _fetch_weather treats any non-empty plausible get_forecasts reply as a successful fetch (_weather_fetch_recovered clears _weather_stale_since) without checking that its rows reach now, so in 5 of 5 cells where the provider keeps returning the same 48 rows and the clock is 1 to 48 h past the last row, the real cycle publishes weather_forecast_stale_hours=None (fresh) while the plan's outdoor array is the last row's 0.7 C held flat (the live weather entity says -3.0 C).
mechanism: coordinator._plausible_forecast_rows filters non-dict rows and out-of-window field values only; a stale-but-well-formed forecast passes, `if forecast_data:` takes the success branch and calls _weather_fetch_recovered, which sets _weather_stale_since=None. _forecast_arrays then extrapolates the last row across the horizon. The empty-forecast and exception branches do mark the data stale (price_weather.py: weather_empty_hidden=0), so the staleness signal exists and only this branch skips it. A weather integration that stops refreshing its forecast (a cached provider, an expired API key that keeps serving the last answer) leaves the plan on a days-old trajectory while the published freshness says nothing is wrong.

evidence.unit: cells (of 5) with every forecast row in the past published as fresh (stale_hours None)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; a count

perturbation.change: --fix: coordinator._plausible_forecast_rows also drops a row whose hour (datetime + 1 h) has ended, patched in memory, so an all-past reply is an empty one and takes the existing stale branch

metric_definition: Of 5 cells 1/6/12/24/48 h past the last row of a non-advancing forecast, cycles publishing weather_forecast_stale_hours None.
phenomenon_property: A feed reply that does not cover now is not a fresh fetch: the forecast's staleness (weather_forecast_stale_hours) is set whenever the forecast the plan stands on no longer reaches the current step, whatever branch delivered it.
seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D1/s2/price_weather.py  (each external feed's success branch -- weather, Tibber, price entity -- driven with a reply that no longer covers now; the price feeds hold, weather does not)

null_control.note: the provider's rows start at the current hour at the same five instants: no cell has every row in the past, stale_hours None is right, outdoor array -4.0 from the live rows

proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py:_fetch_weather: a reply whose rows end before the current step is a failed fetch (_weather_fetch_failed), so stale_hours and the plan's stale marking apply.
